source: made up: person planning their own wedding six weeks out alongside a full workday and lunch vendor calls
persona: Hannah, a product marketing manager getting married on December 5 (six weeks away). Texts rapidly with high energy and occasional exclamation points or mild panic about RSVP stragglers; squeezes vendor calls into her lunch hour and relies on the app to keep wedding admin from swallowing her day job.
situation: Friday morning at 07:00. Working her remote marketing job 09:00–17:30 with a 10:00 product launch sync and 15:00 design review, a 12:30 floral & linen final walkthrough call over lunch, and a 18:30 dance lesson with her fiancé Ben.
life: 07:10 Wake up and text the app: 6 weeks until the wedding!! Help me plan today: morning run & shower before 09:00 work, finish Q4 launch messaging doc and review email copy during work, do the 12:30 florist call and eat lunch, call the hotel room-block manager before 17:00, leave at 18:00 for our 18:30 first-dance lesson, and spend an hour with Ben after dinner chasing down 12 RSVP stragglers.
07:15 Remind the app that vendor phone calls (florist at 12:30 and hotel block manager) have to happen during business hours before 17:00, and the RSVP texts wait until tonight with Ben.
07:20 Go for a 3-mile morning run, shower, and eat a smoothie bowl before logging in at 08:55.
08:58 Report run, shower, and breakfast done. Starting on the Q4 launch messaging doc before my 10:00 sync.
09:00 Draft the Q4 launch messaging doc until 10:00, then join the Product Launch Sync from 10:00 to 11:00.
11:02 Report sync done and continuing the Q4 messaging doc.
11:05 Finish the Q4 launch messaging doc and share it with the director at 12:15.
12:18 Tell the app the Q4 doc is done! Heating up a grain bowl now so I can eat during the 12:30 florist call.
12:30 Zoom call with the wedding florist about table centerpieces and bouquet ribbons while eating lunch; call runs 15 minutes over until 13:15 because of a candelabra rental question.
13:18 Text the app: florist call ran until 13:15, centerpieces are locked in! Now I need to call the hotel room-block manager (takes ~20 mins) before diving into the lifecycle email copy review.
13:20 Call the Marriott room-block coordinator to add 5 more king rooms to the courtesy block, finishing at 13:45.
13:48 Report hotel block extended! Reviewing the 4 lifecycle marketing email drafts before the 15:00 design review.
13:50 Edit and leave comments on the lifecycle email drafts until 14:55.
15:00 Attend the Marketing Design Review meeting until 16:00.

16:05 Sister (maid of honor) calls in a minor panic because her bridesmaid dress hem came back an inch too short from the tailor. Spend 25 minutes on FaceTime looking at shoes with lower heels until 16:30.

16:32 Text the app: maid of honor emergency FaceTime took 30 mins (dress hem drama, solved with lower heels!). Need to finish wrapping up work emails until 17:30, then change clothes before leaving at 18:00 for the dance studio.
16:35 Clear out Friday afternoon Slack messages and finish the email copy sign-off until 17:30.
17:32 Report workday done! Change clothes and touch up makeup before driving with Ben at 18:00 to the ballroom studio.
18:30 Practice the first-dance choreography at the dance lesson until 19:30, then pick up Thai takeout on the way home, arriving at 20:00.
20:05 Report dance lesson done (we didn't step on each other's toes!) and eating Thai takeout with Ben now. Push the RSVP straggler texts to 20:45–21:45.
20:45 Sit on the couch with Ben and the Zola spreadsheet, texting 12 aunts and college friends for their meal choices and updating the seating chart draft until 21:50.
21:55 Report all 12 RSVP stragglers messaged and 7 already replied! Winding down until 23:00.
constraints: Wedding vendor phone calls (florist, hotel room block) must happen during weekday business hours before 17:00.
Must leave the apartment by 18:00 to reach the 18:30 dance lesson on time.
Chasing down RSVP stragglers and working on the seating chart only happens in the evening with her fiancé Ben.
